basic_information.name: OpenAI text-embedding-3 (text-embedding-3-large & text-embedding-3-small)
basic_information.creator: OpenAI (San Francisco, CA)
basic_information.description: OpenAI's third-generation text embedding models, released January 25, 2024, comprising text-embedding-3-large (3072 dimensions) and text-embedding-3-small (1536 dimensions). Both models are trained with Matryoshka Representation Learning (MRL), enabling developers to flexibly reduce embedding dimensions (e.g., to 256, 512, or 1024) via an API parameter while retaining most retrieval accuracy. text-embedding-3-large achieves 64.6% on MTEB and 54.9% on MIRACL (multilingual), a substantial improvement over the previous ada-002 model. These models are the most widely used proprietary embedding API for RAG applications, powering retrieval in ChatGPT, the Assistants API, and thousands of production systems worldwide. Pricing is highly competitive at $0.02/1M tokens (small) and $0.13/1M tokens (large).
basic_information.license: Proprietary (API-only access, no model weights distributed)
basic_information.github_stars: N/A — proprietary API model, no open-source repository. OpenAI's openai-python SDK has ~25,000+ GitHub stars, and OpenAI Cookbook has ~60,000+ stars.

technical_architecture.architecture_type: Cloud API (serverless). Models are hosted on OpenAI's infrastructure and accessed exclusively via REST API. No self-hosting or on-device deployment options. Batch API available for asynchronous high-throughput processing at 50% cost reduction.
technical_architecture.language: Model implementation undisclosed. Client SDKs available in Python (openai), TypeScript/JavaScript (openai-node), .NET, Go, Java, and Rust (community). API follows OpenAI's standard REST interface.
technical_architecture.embedding_dimensions: text-embedding-3-large: default 3072 dimensions (supports Matryoshka reduction to any lower dimension, commonly 256, 512, 1024, 1536). text-embedding-3-small: default 1536 dimensions (supports Matryoshka reduction to any lower dimension, commonly 256, 512). Dimensions controlled via the 'dimensions' parameter in the API request.
technical_architecture.indexing_algorithm: N/A — text-embedding-3 is an embedding generation model, not a vector database. It produces dense vector embeddings that can be indexed with any algorithm (HNSW, IVF, DiskANN, flat, etc.) in any vector store. The Matryoshka training approach uses aggregated loss functions at dimensions {512, 1024, 1536, 3072} for text-embedding-3-large.
technical_architecture.scalability: Serverless API with automatic scaling. Rate limits depend on account tier: Tier 1 starts at 1,000,000 TPM (tokens per minute) for embedding models, scaling up to 10,000,000 TPM at higher tiers. Per-request limit of approximately 300,000 total tokens. Individual input limit of 8,192 tokens per text. Batch API supports up to 50,000 requests per batch file for high-throughput offline processing.
technical_architecture.deployment_options: Cloud API only (api.openai.com). Azure OpenAI Service provides an alternative deployment with enterprise features, data residency (US, Europe, UK, Japan, Canada, South Korea, Singapore, Australia, India, UAE), and VNet integration. No self-hosted, edge, or on-device deployment available. Batch API for asynchronous processing.

rag_specific_capabilities.retrieval_method: Dense vector retrieval only. Models produce dense floating-point embeddings suitable for cosine similarity, dot product, or Euclidean distance search. No native sparse vector (BM25/SPLADE) generation. Hybrid search requires combining with a separate sparse retrieval system. Multi-vector and ColBERT-style late interaction not supported.
rag_specific_capabilities.chunking_strategy_support: N/A — embedding model is agnostic to chunking strategy. Works with any chunking approach. The 8,192-token context window determines maximum chunk size. OpenAI recommends splitting text to fit within this limit. Compatible with all chunking frameworks: LangChain (RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter, SemanticChunker), LlamaIndex (SentenceSplitter), Unstructured, etc.
rag_specific_capabilities.reranking_support: No built-in reranking capability. OpenAI does not offer a dedicated cross-encoder reranking model. Reranking must be implemented via third-party models (Cohere Rerank, cross-encoders from Hugging Face, ColBERT) or LLM-based reranking using GPT models.
rag_specific_capabilities.multimodal_support: Text-only embedding models. No support for images, audio, video, or other modalities. For multimodal embeddings, OpenAI offers CLIP (via open-source model) but not through the embeddings API. Workaround: use GPT-4 Vision to describe images as text, then embed the text descriptions.
rag_specific_capabilities.graph_rag_support: No native graph capabilities. text-embedding-3 produces embeddings only. Knowledge graph construction, entity extraction, and graph-enhanced retrieval must be implemented externally using tools like LlamaIndex's KnowledgeGraphIndex, LangChain's GraphRAG integrations, or Microsoft's GraphRAG framework.
rag_specific_capabilities.citation_grounding: No built-in citation or grounding features in the embedding model itself. Source attribution must be handled at the application layer by tracking document metadata alongside embeddings. The OpenAI Assistants API (which uses these embeddings internally) provides file_citation annotations for grounding.
rag_specific_capabilities.context_window_optimization: Maximum input of 8,192 tokens per embedding request. No built-in text compression or summarization. For documents exceeding this limit, users must implement chunking externally. The Matryoshka dimension reduction feature helps optimize storage and retrieval speed without re-embedding — a form of representation-level optimization rather than context-level.

performance_and_benchmarks.latency: API latency depends on network conditions and server load. Independent benchmarks (Nixie Search, 2024) measured typical single-request latency in the range of 100-500ms for moderate-length inputs. Batch API processes asynchronously with results returned within 24 hours. Latency is higher than locally-hosted embedding models but acceptable for most production RAG applications. [uncertain]
performance_and_benchmarks.throughput: Rate-limited by account tier. Tier 1: 1,000,000 TPM. Tier 5: 10,000,000 TPM. Per-request batch limit: ~300,000 tokens. Batch API supports 50,000 requests per batch file for offline processing at 50% cost. Actual throughput depends on input length; for typical 256-token chunks, Tier 1 allows ~3,900 embeddings/minute. [uncertain]
performance_and_benchmarks.accuracy_metrics: text-embedding-3-large: 64.6% average on MTEB, 54.9% on MIRACL (multilingual). text-embedding-3-small: 62.3% on MTEB, 44.0% on MIRACL. For comparison, the previous ada-002 scored 61.0% on MTEB and 31.4% on MIRACL. At 256 dimensions, text-embedding-3-large still outperforms the full 1536-dimension ada-002 on MTEB. At 1024 dimensions, text-embedding-3-large retains nearly identical performance to the full 3072 dimensions.
performance_and_benchmarks.benchmark_results: MTEB (Massive Text Embedding Benchmark): text-embedding-3-large scores 64.6%, competitive with Cohere embed-v4 (65.2%) but behind Voyage-4 (68.6%) and newer open-source models. MIRACL (multilingual retrieval): 54.9% for large, a 75% improvement over ada-002 (31.4%). BEIR retrieval benchmark: strong performance across diverse retrieval tasks. As of early 2026, text-embedding-3-large ranks in the top tier of proprietary models but has been surpassed by several newer models (Voyage-4, Cohere embed-v4, and top open-source models on MTEB v2 leaderboard).

integration_and_ecosystem.framework_compatibility: Best-in-class framework integration across the AI ecosystem. LangChain (OpenAIEmbeddings class, first-class support), LlamaIndex (OpenAIEmbedding, default embedding provider), Haystack (OpenAITextEmbedder/OpenAIDocumentEmbedder), DSPy (built-in OpenAI embedding support), Microsoft Semantic Kernel (OpenAI connector), Spring AI (OpenAI embedding client), Chroma (built-in OpenAI embedding function), and virtually every RAG framework and vector database provides an OpenAI embedding integration.
integration_and_ecosystem.model_compatibility: Designed to work with any LLM for the generation step of RAG. Most commonly paired with OpenAI's own GPT-4o, GPT-4, and GPT-3.5-turbo, but equally compatible with Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, Mistral, Meta Llama, and any other LLM. The embeddings are standard dense vectors usable with any vector database (Pinecone, Qdrant, Milvus, Weaviate, Chroma, pgvector, Elasticsearch, etc.).
integration_and_ecosystem.mcp_integration_status: OpenAI adopted MCP across its products (ChatGPT desktop, Agents SDK, Responses API) in March 2025. While there is no dedicated MCP server specifically for the embeddings API, OpenAI's broader MCP ecosystem enables connecting to vector stores and embedding workflows via remote MCP servers. Third-party MCP servers wrapping OpenAI embeddings exist in the community.
integration_and_ecosystem.data_source_connectors: N/A — text-embedding-3 is a pure embedding generation API. It accepts text strings and returns vectors. Data source connectivity is handled by orchestration frameworks (LangChain loaders, LlamaIndex readers, Unstructured, Airbyte) that process documents from S3, GCS, Confluence, Notion, Slack, databases, web crawl, etc., then pass text to the embedding API.
integration_and_ecosystem.observability_integration: OpenAI provides a Usage Dashboard for monitoring API consumption (tokens, requests, costs) per model. For deeper tracing: Langfuse, LangSmith, and Arize Phoenix all support OpenAI embedding call instrumentation via their LangChain/LlamaIndex integrations. OpenTelemetry instrumentation available through community packages (opentelemetry-instrumentation-openai). Helicone proxy provides cost tracking and latency monitoring for OpenAI API calls.

pricing_and_cost.pricing_model: Pay-per-token (input tokens only; no output token charges for embeddings). Two pricing tiers: Standard (real-time) and Batch (asynchronous, 50% discount). No subscription or per-seat fees. Volume discounts via higher-tier rate limits as spend increases.
pricing_and_cost.free_tier: OpenAI provides $5 in free API credits for new accounts (covers all API products including embeddings). At $0.02/1M tokens for text-embedding-3-small, $5 covers approximately 250 million tokens of embedding. No perpetual free tier; credits expire after a set period.
pricing_and_cost.cost_at_scale: text-embedding-3-small: $0.02/1M tokens (Standard), $0.01/1M tokens (Batch). text-embedding-3-large: $0.13/1M tokens (Standard), $0.065/1M tokens (Batch). Cost examples: Embedding 1M documents (~500 tokens each = 500M tokens) costs $10 with small or $65 with large (Standard). For 10M documents: $100 (small) or $650 (large). Batch processing halves these costs. Compared to ada-002 ($0.10/1M tokens), text-embedding-3-small is 5x cheaper with better performance.
pricing_and_cost.total_cost_of_ownership: Embedding generation is typically a small fraction of total RAG system cost. For 1M documents with text-embedding-3-small: ~$10 one-time embedding cost + ongoing query embedding costs (negligible for most workloads). Major TCO components: vector database hosting ($20-500+/month depending on scale and provider), LLM generation costs (10-100x more than embedding costs), and infrastructure/engineering time. Using reduced dimensions (e.g., 256 instead of 3072) via Matryoshka saves significantly on vector storage costs (12x less storage). Batch API reduces embedding costs by 50% for non-real-time workloads.

adoption_and_market.market_position: Market leader in proprietary embedding APIs by adoption and mindshare. text-embedding-3 is the default embedding model in most RAG tutorials, courses, and production starters. Dominant position due to OpenAI's brand, ecosystem integration depth, and competitive pricing. However, facing increasing competition from Cohere embed-v4, Voyage AI (now part of Google/Alphabet), and high-quality open-source alternatives (BGE, E5, GTE, Nomic) that match or exceed performance at lower or zero cost.
adoption_and_market.notable_customers: Widely used across the industry — virtually any organization using the OpenAI API for RAG likely uses text-embedding-3. Notable examples include: Thomson Reuters (customer service RAG), Harvard Business School (educational AI chatbot), and thousands of startups building RAG-powered products. The embeddings power retrieval within OpenAI's own products (ChatGPT file search, Assistants API, GPTs with knowledge retrieval). [uncertain]
adoption_and_market.community_size: OpenAI's developer community is the largest in the AI space: 3M+ developers using the API, 350M+ weekly ChatGPT users (broader ecosystem). openai-python SDK: ~25,000 GitHub stars. OpenAI Cookbook: ~60,000+ GitHub stars with extensive embedding tutorials. OpenAI Developer Forum: highly active with thousands of embedding-related discussions. The embedding models benefit from being part of the broader OpenAI ecosystem rather than having a standalone community.
adoption_and_market.funding_and_valuation: OpenAI (the company): valued at $300 billion as of October 2025 funding round. Total funding raised: $17.9 billion+. Latest round: $6.6 billion (October 2024) at $157B valuation, followed by restructuring toward for-profit model. OpenAI is the most well-funded AI company globally. The embedding models are a small but strategically important part of their API revenue, driving developer lock-in to the broader platform.
adoption_and_market.competitive_landscape: Direct competitors: Cohere embed-v4 (65.2% MTEB, multimodal, enterprise-focused), Voyage AI (now Google; Voyage-4 at 68.6% MTEB, strong code/legal domain models), Google Gemini Embedding (integrated with Vertex AI), Amazon Titan Embeddings (AWS ecosystem). Open-source alternatives: BGE (BAAI), E5 (Microsoft), GTE (Alibaba), Nomic Embed, Jina Embeddings — several now match or exceed text-embedding-3-large on MTEB at zero API cost. OpenAI differentiates via: simplest API, deepest framework integration, Matryoshka flexibility, strong multilingual performance, and ecosystem lock-in with GPT models.

entrepreneurial_relevance.startup_applicability: Ideal for: any startup building RAG features that already uses OpenAI's GPT models — adding embeddings is a single API call with zero infrastructure. Best for teams of 1-50 who want to move fast without managing embedding infrastructure. Budget: extremely low entry cost ($0.02/1M tokens for small model means embedding 10,000 documents costs pennies). Use case fit: semantic search, document Q&A, knowledge bases, customer support chatbots, recommendation systems, code search. Consider alternatives when: you need multimodal embeddings (images/audio), domain-specific performance exceeds general-purpose models, cost sensitivity at massive scale favors open-source, or data sovereignty requirements prohibit sending data to OpenAI's API.
entrepreneurial_relevance.build_vs_buy_guidance: Use OpenAI text-embedding-3 (buy) when: speed to market is critical, team lacks ML expertise for model hosting, volume is <100M documents, and data can be sent to OpenAI's API. Consider self-hosted open-source models when: data cannot leave your infrastructure (regulatory/compliance), volume makes API costs prohibitive (>$500/month on embeddings alone), you need domain-specific fine-tuning, or you want to eliminate vendor dependency. Azure OpenAI Service is the middle ground: same models with enterprise compliance, VNet isolation, and data residency guarantees. Migration from OpenAI embeddings to open-source is straightforward but requires re-embedding your entire corpus.
entrepreneurial_relevance.time_to_production: POC: 15-30 minutes (pip install openai + 5 lines of Python). MVP with full RAG pipeline using LangChain/LlamaIndex: 1-3 days. Production deployment: 1-2 weeks including error handling, rate limit management, caching, and monitoring. The fastest path from zero to working RAG system of any embedding option. Azure OpenAI deployment adds 1-2 weeks for enterprise setup.
key_lessons: 1. Start with text-embedding-3-small for prototyping — at $0.02/1M tokens, it is 6.5x cheaper than the large model with only ~2% lower MTEB performance (62.3% vs 64.6%). Switch to large only if retrieval quality measurably improves for your specific use case.

2. Leverage Matryoshka dimensions to optimize cost-performance tradeoff — use 1024 dimensions instead of 3072 for text-embedding-3-large to get nearly identical accuracy with 3x less vector storage cost. Test with 256 dimensions for high-volume, cost-sensitive applications where approximate matching suffices.

3. Use Batch API for initial corpus embedding — the 50% cost discount for non-real-time processing can save hundreds of dollars when embedding large document collections. Reserve Standard API for real-time query embedding only.

4. Plan for vendor lock-in — switching embedding models requires re-embedding your entire corpus (you cannot mix embeddings from different models in the same vector space). Abstract the embedding layer in your code and keep the original text stored alongside vectors to enable future model migration.

5. The embedding model choice matters less than chunking and retrieval strategy — for most startups, optimizing chunk size, overlap, and retrieval (top-k, reranking, hybrid search) will improve RAG quality far more than switching between text-embedding-3-large, Cohere, or Voyage. Invest engineering time in the pipeline, not the model.
entrepreneurial_relevance.no_code_interface: No dedicated no-code interface for the embedding API itself. However, OpenAI's Assistants API and GPTs provide no-code/low-code RAG with built-in file search that uses text-embedding-3-large under the hood. Third-party no-code platforms (Flowise, Dify, AnythingLLM, Relevance AI, Vectara) provide visual RAG builders with OpenAI embedding integration.
entrepreneurial_relevance.session_mapping: Session 1 (AI landscape — introduce embeddings concept), Session 2 (Prompt engineering & tools — hands-on RAG with OpenAI embeddings), Session 3 (AI project framing — Build vs Buy for embedding infrastructure, cost analysis)

confidence.data_quality: High — information sourced from OpenAI's official documentation (platform.openai.com), OpenAI's blog announcement, independent benchmark comparisons (MTEB leaderboard, Pinecone, DataCamp, Ailog), pricing calculators (Helicone, CostGoat), and community discussions on OpenAI Developer Forum.
confidence.cross_reference: MTEB scores (64.6% large, 62.3% small) confirmed across OpenAI blog, MTEB Hugging Face leaderboard, and multiple independent comparisons (Ailog, Agentset, Openxcell). Pricing confirmed across OpenAI pricing page, Helicone calculator, and CostGoat calculator. Matryoshka dimension behavior confirmed by Pinecone, Supabase, Weaviate, and Azure SQL documentation. Max token limit (8,192) confirmed across OpenAI docs and community reports.
confidence.caveats: MTEB scores are from the original MTEB v1 benchmark (January 2024 evaluation); newer MTEB v2 leaderboard uses different methodology and models may rank differently. text-embedding-3 models have been surpassed by several newer models (Voyage-4, Cohere embed-v4, top open-source models) since their January 2024 release — OpenAI has not released a v4 embedding model as of February 2026. Latency and throughput figures are estimates based on independent benchmarks, not official OpenAI guarantees. The per-request token limit of ~300,000 is community-reported and not officially documented.
confidence.security_posture: OpenAI API platform is SOC 2 Type 2 certified (latest report: January-June 2025). Data encryption at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.2+). API data is NOT used for model training by default. Data Processing Addendum (DPA) available for GDPR compliance. Data residency options via Azure OpenAI (US, Europe, UK, Japan, etc.). Known risks: embedding vectors can theoretically be inverted to approximate original text (embedding inversion attacks), though this is a general embedding model risk, not specific to OpenAI. Zero data retention option available for enterprise customers. No on-premise deployment means data must leave customer infrastructure (mitigated by Azure OpenAI VNet integration).
